The Police Sub-Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the above named accused persons alleging that they have committed the offencess punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The complainant has filed this complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C.
On hearing of the complainant my Predecessor referred the matter for investigation acting under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.
The Investigation Officer has conducted investigation and filed his Final Report.
3. It is the case of the complainant that during the year 2000, they came in contact with accused No.2 who was engaged in Kanava Marketing.
This accused No.2 had taken the complainant to the Office of M/s.Sarathi TradeImpex India Ltd.
The accused No.2 represented himself as a Chairman and MD of the said company and accused No.3 and 4 are the Directors.
Accused No.5 to 8 are also part of the said company.
They involved in the business of development and sale of lands.
They had entered into an Agreement in respect of Sy.No.43/1.
This accused No.2 in furtherance of his act had taken the complainant to the said land by saying that the said land actually belongs to their company and they are forming private layouts.
They induced the complainant to pay an amount of Rs.12,00,000/-.
They have promised that they will give proportionate share and profit to the complainant.
The complainant has paid the amount through the cheque.
This complainant on doubt has conducted enquiry and came to know that the said land is not belongs to the accused and their company.
The complainant had been to the accused and requested to return back the said amount paid by him.
The accused threatened to murder him if he goes on claiming the said amount.
He had been to the Police Station and lodged the information against the accused.
But, the Police have not taken any action and in turn these accused have issued postdated cheque on the words of the Police.
But however all these cheques were dishonoured.
The accused have committed the offences punishable under Section 420, 468, 196, 506 and 120B of IPC.
On these grounds, the matter was referred to the SHO and the Final Report was submitted against the accused.
4. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.370/2014 at Jayanagar Police Station.
Accused No.1 was arrested and produced before this Court and enlarged on bail.
As per order dated 14.03.2023 accused No.1 was reported dead.
Hence, the case against accused No.1 was Abated.

On completion of the investigation, the Police Inspector of Jayanagar Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against accused No.2 alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to accused No.2.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to accused No.2 under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that accused No.2 has committed the offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences has been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.

To prove the charges framed against accused No.2, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of PW1 to PW3 and the documentary evidences in Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

After completion of the prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling accused No.2 personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined accused No.2 under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.
6. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for accused No.2.
Perused the materials available on record.
7. The points for determination are:-

1. Whether the Prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubts that accused No.2 has committed the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code?
2. What order or sentence?

8. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following:-
 REASONS 9. POINT No.1 :- It is the case of the complainant/Prosecution that the accused No.2 represented himself as a Chairman and MD of M/s.Sarathi TradeImpex India Ltd.
They have engaged in the development and sale of lands.
In the name of development and sale of lands, they have taken huge amount of Rs.12,00,000/- from the complainant and have not repaid.
10. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 Muniraju wherein this witness has deposed that the accused No.1 was a Marketing Manager of Kanava Marketing.
He was also working as a Marketing Executive.
He has resigned to the Kanava Marketing and he had joined as a Manager of some other Garment company.
During the year 2012, he came in contact with accused No.1 through CW6.
He had been to their Office formed in the name and style as M/s.Sarathi Trade Impex India Ltd.
He was informed that they are engaged in manufacturing of pants and shirts and requested him to work as a full time Manager of the said company.
He was also told that these accused were also conducting the business in the name and style of Sarathi Holidays to the foreigners.
They were sending the Directors to the foreign trips.
He was requested to come to the foreign along with other Directors of the company.
Further he was informed that they are developing the lands situated at Hosadoddi Village in Sy.No.43/1.
They have purchased 1 acre 8 guntas of land.
They have taken him to the said land.
He was told that they have purchased the said land for an amount of Rs.1,20,00,000/- and requested him to invest his amount.

But, however they refused to repay and in turn they have threatened him to murder him.
They have issued postdated cheques.
But, however all the cheques were dishonoured.
11. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW5/PW2 Mr.Rajesh who has deposed that he was working in the company by name Sarathi Holidays as an Accountant.
CW6 to CW9 were the promoters of the said company.
He has deposited an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to the said company.
CW6, CW7 and CW9 have also deposited their amounts.
Later, he came out of the company and further has deposed that he is not aware of the negotiation between the complainant and accused.
He has turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
12. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW8/PW3 Appaji.
He has also deposed that he has invested an amount of Rs.25,000/- to the said company.
But, he also came out of the company and deposed ignorance of the negotiations of the complainant and the accused.
He has also turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
13. It is the case of the Prosecution that late accused No.1 along with accused No.2 have cheated the complainant and taken huge amount of Rs.12,00,000/-.
On convincing him that they have already purchased the land bearing Sy.No.43/1 situated at Hosadoddi Village, Ramanagara District.
He was convinced that they will share the profit after development of the said land.
But, later, he found that accused No.1 and 2 have not purchased the said land and he was cheated by them.
14. The Prosecution has examined CW1/PW2 wherein this witness has deposed that he was the Ex-Manager of Kanava Marketing and the accused was the Executive Manager of the said company.
He left the company and joined the new company wherein he was deputed as a Chief Manager.
In his evidence he has deposed that these accused in-charged him of their entire company wherein they are manufacturing pants and shirts.
The complainant was In-charge of sale of the manufacturing of pants and t-shirts of the accused company.
Later he was told that these accused have purchased the property in Sy.No.43/1.
He has invested an amount of Rs.12,00,000/-.
These accused promised him to share the profit.
But however he found that these accused have not all purchased the said land.
CW5 and CW8 have turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
The only evidence available before this Court is the evidence of CW1.
This CW1 in his evidence has deposed that Ex.P4 is the Receipt for the payment of Rs.20,00,000/- to the late accused No.1.
He has specifically admitted that the signature of accused No.2 has not at all being found in the Receipt Ex.P4 or Ex.P5.
Further he has also admitted that in respect of the said matter he has already lodged the information against this accused No.1 and 2 as per Ex.P6.
Further, this witness in his cross-examination has deposed that he has personally witnessed the Agreement of Sale executed in favour of this accused No.1 and 2.
Whereas, this witness in his evidence has deposed that the said property was not at all agreed to sell by the original owner to the accused No.1 and 2.
Accused No.1 has paid the amount as per the Agreement of Sale.

CW1 has further deposed that the said Agreement of Sale was not at all handed over to the Investigation Officer to show that this accused No.1 has entered into an Agreement with the original owner of the said property.

4 examine CW1 only.
CW5 and CW8 have turned hostile to the case of the Prosecution.
CW1 has made several improvements in his evidence.
This informant has even lodged one more information against the accused which is pending for trial and again he has lodged this information.
Absolutely there is no evidence to prove the guilt of the accused No.2 beyond all reasonable doubts.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

15. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubts.
Therefore, accused No.2 is not found guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS
Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.1 is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 323, 420 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bonds and surety bond executed under Section 437 of Cr.P.C. will be canceled after appeal period.
